narrative_purpose: An oblique, label-ready atoll wake makes the island mass effect visible without claiming that it has been measured at Awa'atlu.
subject: A low alien atoll rising from a steep submarine pedestal in an otherwise clear dark-blue ocean. A broad current approaches from the left, separates around the island, and forms two curling downstream eddies. Beneath the surface, pale internal density layers bend upward against the steep slope. A soft living-teal plankton plume appears only in the downstream wake, with a compact fish school at its outer edge.
scene: Open tropical Eastern-Sea-like water around an isolated inhabited reef island, seen as a transparent oblique cutaway from high above.
camera: High three-quarter aerial-oblique view with the island just right of center, upstream water on the left and a long wake extending to the lower right.
light: Soft cyan daylight on the island rim, deep indigo offshore water, and a restrained living-teal glow tracing the biologically active wake.
palette: Void-indigo open ocean, ocean teal shallows, cyan rim light, living-teal wake and sparse magenta reef accents.
style: Painterly naturalist ocean-process plate with atmospheric depth, not a satellite photograph or vector flowchart.
detail_level: Clear island pedestal, two wake eddies, bent subsurface layers and one biological plume; upstream water remains simple and empty.
composition: Island as the obstacle, upstream and downstream regions clearly distinguishable, with dark negative space beside the slope and eddies for callout labels.
consistency_notes: Match the marine architecture of fig-00 and fig-01. Render current structure through suspended particles and curved density bands, never arrows.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no map legend, no satellite photo, no flat infographic, no glossy CGI, no giant storm vortex
